title: Diversity of Living Things
seo_title: Grade 11 Biology (SBI3U): Diversity of Living Things Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Classification and taxonomy: the three domains and six kingdoms; binomial nomenclature and the taxonomic ranks; dichotomous keys; the characteristics of bacteria, archaea, viruses, protists, fungi, plants and animals; and the importance of biodiversity. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Biology, Grade 11, University Preparation (SBI3U), Strand B: Diversity of Living Things)
meta_desc: Free Grade 11 Biology (SBI3U) worksheets on the diversity of living things: taxonomy, binomial names, domains and kingdoms, bacteria and viruses, protists, fungi, plants and animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are grouped by shared features and evolutionary history.
key_sub: Domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species.
body_html:
How to think about it

Biologists sort the huge variety of life into groups that share features and ancestry. The ranks go from broad to narrow: domain, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species. Every species has a two-part scientific name, the genus and the species, written in italics (Acer saccharum, the sugar maple).

The three domains are Bacteria, Archaea (both prokaryotes, with no nucleus) and Eukarya (cells with a nucleus). Eukarya includes protists, fungi, plants and animals. Viruses are not placed in any kingdom: they are not cells and can only reproduce inside a host cell.

Example

Which two ranks make up a scientific name?

Binomial nomenclature uses the genus and the species.

Answer: genus and species

Example

A cell has no nucleus and lives in a hot spring. Which domains are possible?

No nucleus means prokaryote.

Answer: Bacteria or Archaea

Common mistakes

  • Writing the genus with a small letter or not using italics.
  • Calling viruses bacteria: viruses are not cells.
  • Thinking that fungi are plants: fungi do not photosynthesize and have chitin cell walls.

items.q: Why is reproduction not a defining property of living things?
c: some living organisms, such as mules and worker bees, cannot reproduce
items.e: Metabolism and cellular organization are defining.

items.q: Which description fits kingdom Animalia?
c: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food
multicellular eukaryotes with a cellulose cell wall that make their own food
prokaryotic, mostly unicellular, with a cell wall of peptidoglycan
items.e: Animalia: multicellular eukaryotes with no cell wall that ingest food.

items.q: What is the genetic material of bacteriophages usually?
items.e: Plant viruses usually have single-stranded RNA.

items.q: What are prions?
c: abnormally folded proteins that cause disease
items.e: e.g. mad cow disease (BSE).

items.q: How should a scientific name be written when printed?
c: in italics, genus with a capital letter and species epithet in small letters
with both words capitalized in plain type
items.e: e.g. Mangifera indica.

items.e: Fungi: heterotrophic eukaryotes with a cell wall of chitin.
